subject: Geography
description: Major currents (Gulf Stream / Kuroshio / Humboldt), planetary winds

questions.stem: The WARM ocean current along the east coast of North America is the:
questions.explanation: Gulf Stream — warm, flows NE from Gulf of Mexico along US east coast, crosses Atlantic as North Atlantic Drift, moderates climate of NW Europe. Labrador Current — cold, flows south past Canada (icebergs from Titanic). Canary Current — cold off W Africa. California Current — cold off US west coast.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The planetary winds that blow from SUB-TROPICAL HIGH toward the EQUATORIAL LOW are called:
questions.explanation: Trade winds — NE trades (Northern Hemisphere) and SE trades (Southern Hemisphere) driven by Coriolis. Converge at ITCZ (Intertropical Convergence Zone) near equator = the Doldrums. Westerlies blow from 30°-60° toward the polar low. Polar easterlies from 90° toward 60°.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the OCEAN CURRENT with its WATER-TEMP CHARACTER. A. Kuroshio.  B. Humboldt (Peru).  C. Benguela.  D. Agulhas. List-II: 1. Warm (N Pacific, east of Japan).  2. Cold (west coast of S America).  3. Cold (west coast of S Africa).  4. Warm (east coast of S Africa).
questions.explanation: Kuroshio ('black tide', Pacific analogue of the Gulf Stream) — warm. Humboldt — cold, supports rich Peruvian anchovy fishery; El Niño disrupts it. Benguela — cold, off Namibia. Agulhas — warm, off east S Africa.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The deflection of winds and ocean currents due to Earth's rotation is caused by the:
questions.explanation: Coriolis effect — apparent force due to Earth's rotation. Deflects moving objects TO THE RIGHT in Northern Hemisphere, TO THE LEFT in Southern. Strongest at poles, zero at equator. Explains trade winds, cyclone rotation.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The world's LARGEST cold ocean current is:

options.option_text: West Wind Drift / Antarctic Circumpolar Current

questions.explanation: Antarctic Circumpolar Current (also West Wind Drift) — the largest current on Earth, circling Antarctica clockwise (from W→E). Transports ~100-150 million cubic metres of water per second — more than any other ocean current.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which winds are also called the 'ROARING FORTIES'?
questions.explanation: Strong westerlies between 40° S and 50° S latitudes. 'Roaring Forties', 'Furious Fifties', 'Screaming Sixties' denote progressively stronger winds. Driven by lack of large landmasses to break the flow in the Southern Ocean.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The meeting of warm and cold ocean currents near Newfoundland creates ideal conditions for:

options.option_text: Dense fog and one of the world's richest fishing grounds

questions.explanation: Warm Gulf Stream meets cold Labrador Current near Newfoundland → water column mixing brings nutrients to surface → phytoplankton bloom → plankton-feeder fish population → apex fisheries. The Grand Banks historically were among the world's most productive cod fisheries. The same meeting also causes thick fogs — the 1912 Titanic iceberg drifted south here.
